mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 4 Series 418i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 4 Series 418i engine replacement typically costs £1,200-£2,200 for a used unit, £2,200-£3,800 for a reconditioned engine, and £2,800-£4,500 for a fully rebuilt B38B15A with warranty. Supply-only prices exclude fitting - budget an additional £500-£900 for specialist labour.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 4 Series 418i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a metallic rattling noise from the engine, especially during cold starts. As the problem worsens, you may notice poor engine performance, a check engine light, or in severe cases, the engine may fail to start or suffer catastrophic damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 4 Series 418i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's value and condition. With a typical 418i valued at £6,000-£14,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,800-£4,500 represents a significant but often justifiable investment - especially if the car is otherwise in good condition. For cars at the lower end of the value range, a timing chain repair (£1,500-£2,200) may be the more sensible option.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 4 Series 418i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 4 Series 418i engine replacement takes 1-2 days for a specialist workshop, assuming the replacement engine is already available. The B38 is a relatively compact three-cylinder unit, making access simpler than larger BMW engines.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 418i and 420i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 418i uses a 1.5-litre three-cylinder B38B15A engine producing 136hp, while the 420i uses a 2.0-litre four-cylinder B48 engine producing 184hp. The 420i offers significantly more power and refinement, but the 418i delivers better fuel economy and lower running costs.

mainEntity.name: Does a replacement BMW 4 Series 418i engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt and reconditioned BMW 4 Series 418i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically carry a shorter warranty (30-90 days), so always confirm the terms with your chosen supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 4 Series 418i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 4 Series 418i was introduced as the entry-level petrol variant in the 4 Series range, offering a more accessible point of entry to the premium coupe and Gran Coupe body styles. Throughout its production run, the 418i was powered exclusively by BMW's B38 three-cylinder petrol engine, a turbocharged 1.5-litre unit that prioritised efficiency while delivering adequate performance for everyday driving.

milestones.description: F32/F33 418i launched with B38B15A 1.5L three-cylinder turbo petrol, 136hp
F36 Gran Coupe 418i joins the range with the same B38B15A engine
LCI (Life Cycle Impulse) facelift introduced across the 4 Series range; 418i continues with B38B15A now featuring OPF (petrol particulate filter) for Euro 6 emissions compliance
F32/F33/F36 generation ends; 418i nameplate discontinued for G22 generation

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 4 Series 418i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 4 Series 418i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 4 Series 418i is powered exclusively by the B38B15A 1.5-litre three-cylinder turbo petrol engine. While generally considered a reliable unit, it has a few known weak points that typically emerge from around 60,000 miles onwards. Rebuilt B38 engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the BMW 4 Series 418i B38 Engine Develops Rattling Noises
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can wear prematurely, allowing the chain to slacken. This produces a metallic rattling noise, particularly noticeable during cold starts. If ignored, chain slack can lead to timing misalignment and, in severe cases, catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early and chain hasn't stretched

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New chain, tensioner, guides, and VANOS units
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if rattling has been present for some time
Best when chain has failed or engine has suffered collateral damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 4 Series 418i (2014-2018) is currently valued at approximately £6,000-£14,000 depending on mileage, condition, and body style (Coupe vs Gran Coupe) `[THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader 2025]`. With a rebuilt engine costing £2,800-£4,500 supply-only, replacement cost represents roughly 20-75% of vehicle value. For lower-value examples approaching the £6,000 mark, a timing chain repair may be the more sensible option; for cars valued above £10,000, a full replacement is comfortably justified.
problems.recommendation: If you catch the timing chain tensioner wear early - a rattle only on cold start that disappears as the engine warms up - a tensioner replacement or full timing chain kit is the sensible, cost-effective route. However, if the chain has already slipped or the engine has suffered damage, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty is the safer long-term investment. The B38 is generally robust, so don't write the car off prematurely - get a specialist diagnosis first.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B38B15A BMW 4 Series 418i engine prices

problems.h4: Cooling System Failures - Water Pump & Thermostat Housing Leaks
problems.rootCause: The B38 engine's water pump and thermostat housing are known to develop leaks over time. The turbocharger also has coolant lines sealed with rubber O-rings that can perish, leading to coolant loss.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught before overheating occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace O-rings or entire coolant pipes
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if coolant smell or visible leak from turbo area
Only if engine has overheated and sustained damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See above - a typical 418i values at £6,000-£14,000. Cooling system repairs are relatively modest compared to the vehicle's value and are almost always worth doing rather than replacing the engine.
problems.recommendation: Cooling system issues on the B38 are well-understood and generally inexpensive to fix relative to the value of the car. If you catch a leak early, replace the water pump and thermostat housing preventatively. These are wear items, not design flaws. Keep a close eye on coolant levels - regular checks are the best prevention against overheating damage.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your BMW 4 Series 418i
finalCta.paragraph: The B38 engine in the 418i is fundamentally a reliable unit, but like any modern turbocharged engine, it has known weak points that emerge with age and mileage. Catching timing chain tensioner wear or coolant leaks early can save you thousands. If the worst happens, EnginesMarket connects you with vetted UK specialists who can supply a rebuilt B38 with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty - at a fraction of main dealer prices. Don't scrap a good car over a fixable engine issue.
